mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1.5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Empirical 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from a zero return baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during the identified rising rate period.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly declines by more than 0.2% in a month, it signals a cooling inflationary pressure that prompts risk-on sentiment and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the CPI beat (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both unemployment rate (UNRATE) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a labor market transition toward expansion, which elevates corporate earnings expectations and pushes S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases while INDPRO increases in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) during the identified labor transition signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the prior quarter's average accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests strengthening demand for housing, which is associated with higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly value > previous quarter average AND UNRATE monthly change < -0.1%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show no significant positive deviation from historical averages during the signal window (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 2% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing capacity, which raises the risk of supply shocks and is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly < -2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain non-negative during the contraction (cumulative return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of RSAFS to GDP (implied credit availability) exceeds 50% for two months in a row during a rising interest rate environment, it suggests tighter credit conditions that suppress equity risk pricing and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS / GDP > 0.5 for two consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS > 1.0%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) despite the credit ratio signal.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected drop in the monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) relative to the prior month's estimate accompanied by a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2% signals a weakening labor market, which can trigger a risk-off reaction and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly < prior month estimate AND UNRATE monthly change > 0.2%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05) when the labor signal is present.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for 4 consecutive months in a low-rate environment creates a risk that the Federal Reserve holds rates steady longer than expected, which can result in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly < 3% for four consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 1.5%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when the inflation signal is active (IC > 0.1).
